title: J&J's Oral Psoriasis Drug Logged 18,000 Prescriptions in Its First Full Quarter. Is It Coming for Injectables?
summary: ICOTYDE logged more than 18,000 prescriptions in its first full quarter. The oral IL-23R peptide has earned entry into the high-efficacy psoriasis market, but durable value still depends on paid fills, persistence, payer quality, safety, and additional indications.
source_status: Published publicly on Facebook; this complete English edition preserves the argument sequence, denominator caveats, commercial analysis, references and disclaimer

core_judgments: Eighteen thousand prescriptions show willingness to try a high-efficacy oral option, but they do not by themselves establish paid revenue or long-term persistence.

ICOTYDE outperformed deucravacitinib head to head and has supportive one-year maintenance evidence, but responder-denominator results cannot be compared directly with whole-population rates from other trials.
J&J's more-than-$5-billion ambition requires success across indications as well as durable reimbursement, refills, safety, and real-world outcomes.
